acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Configuration screen displays three tabs: General, Persona Models, Model Registry
The General tab contains all existing settings (auto_handoff_enabled, max_handoff_depth, capture_dialogues, auto_archive_days, ledger_root) with identical save behavior
Tab switching re-renders only the tab content area, not the full page
Switching tabs when unsaved changes exist triggers a confirmation dialog with Discard / Stay options
Tab CSS uses `.config-tabs` / `.config-tab` class names, visually identical to `.knowledge-tabs` / `.knowledge-tab` styling
Placeholder stubs exist for Persona Models and Model Registry tabs (display a "Coming soon" message or empty state)

summary: Rewrote config.js from a single 79-line renderConfig() function into a tabbed view with module-level state management. Added three tabs: General, Persona Models, Model Registry. Tab switching re-renders only #config-tab-content (not the full page). Unsaved-changes guard uses confirm() with Discard/Stay semantics and resets dirty state on Discard or after a successful save. renderConfig() now loads API.getModels/getPersonas/getAssignments in parallel with API.getConfig() via Promise.all, falling back gracefully when those API methods don't yet exist. Stub tabs for Persona Models and Model Registry render 'Coming soon' empty-state cards. Added .config-tabs / .config-tab CSS to styles.css, mirroring .knowledge-tabs / .knowledge-tab exactly (same flex layout, border-bottom track, margin-bottom overlap, --color-ready active state).

comments.note: config.js now uses module-level vars (configActiveTab, configDirty) in the global scope — consistent with the rest of the SPA (e.g. knowledge.js uses a similar pattern). If the SPA grows, consider namespacing these under a ConfigView object to avoid potential global name collisions.

The dirty-tracking listeners in wireGeneralTabEvents() use both 'change' and 'input' events to cover all input types (checkboxes fire 'change', text inputs fire 'input'). This is intentional and correct, but worth documenting in a comment for the next developer.

The tab-switch dirty guard uses the native window.confirm() dialog, matching the existing SPA pattern (no custom modal library). If a custom modal system is introduced in future (e.g. for WP-008/009), this should be upgraded to use it for visual consistency.

styles.css uses a flat append strategy — new view-specific CSS is added to the bottom. The file is now ~3090 lines. A section-based structure (one CSS section per view) would improve navigability; consider a future cleanup pass.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified by static code analysis and runtime regression testing. Full test suite (117 files, 3523 tests) passes with zero regressions. All AC met: three tabs render correctly, General tab contains all five settings with correct save behavior, tab switching only re-renders #config-tab-content, dirty guard uses confirm() with Discard/Stay semantics, .config-tabs/.config-tab CSS is property-for-property identical to .knowledge-tabs/.knowledge-tab, stub tabs display 'Coming soon' messages. One medium-priority UX edge case noted (configDirty persistence after SPA navigation) — not an AC violation, noted as improvement comment.

comments.note: configDirty flags (configDirty.general etc.) are never reset on renderConfig() re-entry. Scenario: user makes changes, navigates away WITHOUT saving, then navigates back to config. configDirty.general remains true. Immediately switching tabs triggers the 'You have unsaved changes' dialog spuriously, even though the page just re-fetched fresh config data from the server. Fix: reset all configDirty values to false at the start of renderConfig() or renderConfigPage(). Not an AC violation since WP-007 AC only requires the guard fires when unsaved changes exist within a page session.

wireGeneralTabEvents() attaches both 'change' and 'input' event listeners to the form. This is intentional (checkboxes fire 'change', text inputs fire 'input'). Consider adding a brief code comment explaining this dual-listener pattern for future developers maintaining the dirty-tracking logic.

No existing jsdom test suite covers config.js rendering. Future WPs that extend the config view (WP-008, WP-009) may benefit from adding a client-rendering test for config.js using the same vm.runInThisContext pattern used in tests/gui/client-rendering.test.ts.

summary: PASS with Fix-Forward. All six AC met. Code is clean, well-structured, and correctly decomposed into seven named functions with clear extension points for WP-008/009. Applied two Fix-Forward edits: (1) added configDirty reset at the top of renderConfigPage() to prevent spurious unsaved-changes dialogs after SPA navigation away and back to /config; (2) added an explanatory comment on the dual 'change'/'input' listener pattern in wireGeneralTabEvents(). CSS mirror is property-for-property identical to .knowledge-tabs/.knowledge-tab. Input validation and escapeHtml usage are correct throughout. Module-level globals are consistent with the existing SPA pattern; namespacing under a ConfigView object is a low-priority long-term improvement flagged as tech debt (pre-existing pattern, not introduced here). One documentation-forward item tagged for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: Added configDirty reset block at the top of renderConfigPage(). When the router calls renderConfig(app) on re-navigation to /config, fresh server data is fetched and the scaffold is rebuilt. Any configDirty flags left true from a previous visit were causing the 'You have unsaved changes' confirm dialog to fire spuriously on the first tab switch of the new visit. The fix (three lines resetting all three flags) is non-behavioral for the normal session path but eliminates the UX defect on re-entry. QA regression suite remains valid — the guard still fires correctly when the user actually makes changes within a page session.

Expanded the comment on the dual 'change'/'input' listeners in wireGeneralTabEvents() to explicitly explain why both events are registered: checkboxes fire 'change' (not 'input'), text/number inputs fire 'input' on each keystroke. This prevents a future developer from removing one listener as a 'duplicate'. The Developer and QA both flagged this gap; resolved inline.

configActiveTab and configDirty are module-level globals — consistent with how the rest of this SPA was built pre-WP-007 (e.g., project-list.js, orchestrator.js also use globals). The asymmetry with knowledge.js (which uses closure-local vars) is pre-existing and not introduced by this WP. Long-term: consider namespacing all view-level state under view objects (ConfigView, KnowledgeView, etc.) to prevent collisions as the SPA grows. Not blocking.

[documentation-forward] config.js module-level doc comment lists dependencies as 'API, escapeHtml, showLoading, showError' but also uses UI.card() (from components.js) and window.confirm(). The dependency list should include 'UI' to match the pattern in knowledge.js and project-detail.js, so future developers know to include components.js before config.js.

summary: Addressed all documentation gaps for WP-007 (tabbed Configuration screen).
1. Fixed config.js module-level doc comment: added 'UI' to the Depends on list (resolves documentation-forward item from code review).

2. Added section 11 'Configuration Page Classes' to ui-components.md documenting .config-tabs and .config-tab CSS classes, with a note that only #config-tab-content is re-rendered on tab switch. Renumbered all subsequent sections (old 11→12 through old 17→18).

3. Added 'config.js — Internal Functions' subsection to api-surface.md §2.7 documenting all seven named functions (renderConfig, renderConfigPage, renderConfigTabContent, renderGeneralTab, wireGeneralTabEvents, renderPersonaModelsTab stub, renderModelRegistryTab stub), the module-level state variables (configActiveTab, configDirty), and the full dependency list.
4. Regenerated all CTX .context/ files via 'ctx generate' — 36 files rebuilt cleanly.

comments.note: The documentation-forward item from code review (config.js dependency list missing 'UI') was resolved inline in the source file comment rather than only in the manifest — this keeps the canonical dependency declaration co-located with the code.

The config.js internal function table in api-surface.md explicitly flags renderPersonaModelsTab and renderModelRegistryTab as stubs with notes pointing to WP-008 and WP-009 respectively, making extension points discoverable to future developers.

notes: config.js is now ~200 lines, split into clearly named functions: renderConfig (entry, parallel load), renderConfigPage (scaffold + tab-bar wiring), renderConfigTabContent (dispatcher), renderGeneralTab (HTML), wireGeneralTabEvents (event listeners), renderPersonaModelsTab (stub), renderModelRegistryTab (stub).

Module-level vars configActiveTab and configDirty persist across tab switches within the same page visit. They are intentionally not reset on renderConfig() re-entry — if the page is navigated away from and back, the SPA will call renderConfig(app) again which re-fetches all data and re-renders the scaffold, but configActiveTab will restore to the previously active tab, which is desirable UX.
API.getModels / API.getPersonas / API.getAssignments are guarded with optional-chaining fallbacks (Promise.resolve([])) so the page works now before WP-008/WP-009 add those API methods.

WP-008 (Persona Models tab) and WP-009 (Model Registry tab) should replace the stub return values of renderPersonaModelsTab() and renderModelRegistryTab() respectively — no other function needs to change.

All 6 AC verified PASS. Full regression suite clean (3523 tests). One medium-priority UX improvement identified: configDirty state persists across SPA navigation — user returning to config page after unsaved-then-abandoned changes will see a spurious dirty dialog. Not blocking for code review, but worth a fix-forward. config.js is clean, well-structured, ~204 lines. CSS mirror is exact. Ready for code review.

PASS with two Fix-Forward edits applied to config.js (configDirty reset on re-entry; dual-listener explanatory comment). All 6 AC confirmed met. One documentation-forward item: the module-level comment in config.js should add 'UI' to its dependency list (uses UI.card() but doesn't declare it). CSS is correct and requires no documentation. WP-008 and WP-009 extension points are clearly stubbed — renderPersonaModelsTab() and renderModelRegistryTab() are the only functions those WPs need to replace.
